rules.rule: Goods sold by description must correspond with the description; where sale is by both sample and description, correspondence with the sample alone is insufficient.
rules.plain_language: Compare the actual bulk with both the agreed description and any sample term that forms part of the contract.
rules.scenario_relevance: The buyer alleges thread-count mismatch against the description and approved sample.

rules.topic: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness
rules.rule: The Act sets out limited circumstances in which conditions as to quality or fitness are implied, including specified-purpose reliance and merchantable quality in relevant sales by description, subject to the statutory qualifications.
rules.plain_language: A defect does not automatically prove every implied quality term; consider the conditions in the section, the sale and any examination.
rules.scenario_relevance: Colour bleeding and quality issues need to be assessed against the sale terms and statutory conditions.

rules.rule: A sale is by sample where the contract has an express or implied term to that effect; the section includes conditions relating to correspondence of bulk with sample and the buyer's opportunity to compare.
rules.plain_language: An approved sample matters legally when it is a contractual sample, and the statutory conditions and facts still need review.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project says the batch did not match an approved sample, but the contract must be checked to establish the sample term and consequences.

rules.rule: No property in unascertained goods transfers to the buyer until the goods are ascertained.
rules.plain_language: First determine whether the goods were identified as the contract goods.
rules.scenario_relevance: The 500 saris' identification and allocation to the order are not described in detail.

rules.rule: For specific or ascertained goods, property passes when the parties intend; intention is assessed from the contract terms, conduct and circumstances, subject to statutory rules.
rules.plain_language: There is no universal ownership-transfer point for every sale.
rules.scenario_relevance: The order terms, identification of goods, delivery terms and conduct are missing, so ownership timing cannot be concluded.

rules.topic: Risk prima facie passes with property
rules.rule: Unless otherwise agreed, risk prima facie follows property, subject to the Act's provisions and exceptions.
rules.plain_language: Risk needs to be considered with ownership and the parties' agreement, not assumed from shipment alone.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project lacks delivery/risk terms and evidence about when property passed.

rules.rule: A buyer who has not previously examined delivered goods is not deemed to have accepted them until a reasonable opportunity to examine conformity; the seller must afford a reasonable opportunity on request when tendering delivery unless otherwise agreed.
rules.plain_language: Examination is relevant to whether the buyer has accepted goods.
rules.scenario_relevance: The London buyer's inspector reportedly examined and rejected the shipment; timing and communications matter.

rules.rule: Acceptance can occur when the buyer communicates acceptance, acts inconsistently with the seller's ownership after delivery, or retains goods beyond a reasonable time without rejecting them.
rules.plain_language: Acceptance depends on what the buyer communicated or did and the time allowed by the circumstances.
rules.scenario_relevance: The buyer's inspection and rejection timing need to be confirmed.

rules.rule: Unless otherwise agreed, a buyer with a right to refuse goods is not bound to return them; communicating refusal is sufficient under this section.
rules.plain_language: This section concerns return of goods after a valid refusal; it does not itself decide whether a right to refuse existed.
rules.scenario_relevance: First determine whether the buyer had a right to reject under the contract and relevant statutory rules.
